title: Linearization of a product-preserving set-valued vector-space functor
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. Let $\mathrm{Vect}^{\mathrm{fd}}_k$ denote the category of finite-dimensional $k$-vector spaces and $k$-linear maps, and let $L:\mathrm{Vect}^{\mathrm{fd}}_k\to\mathrm{Sets}$ be a covariant functor (it preserves identities and composition). Suppose $L(0)$ is a singleton and, for every $U,V$, the comparison $c_{U,V}=(L(p_U),L(p_V)):L(U\oplus V)\to L(U)\times L(V)$ induced by the projections is bijective. There is a unique choice of $k$-vector space structures on the sets $L(V)$ such that every $L(f)$ is linear and $L(f+g)=L(f)+L(g)$, $L(af)=aL(f)$ for all parallel linear maps $f,g$ and all $a\in k$; equivalently these choices lift $L$ to a $k$-linear functor into all $k$-vector spaces [def-weil-linear-functor]. Its operations are $0_{L(V)}=L(0\to V)(*)$, $x+y=L(+_V)c_{V,V}^{-1}(x,y)$, and $a x=L(a\,\mathrm{id}_V)(x)$, where $+_V:V\oplus V\to V$ is addition. The maps $c_{U,V}$ are then linear isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 06I6 (lemma-linear-functor), specialized to finite-dimensional vector spaces over a field.

proof.text:
Write $z_V=L(0\to V)(*)$, $q_{U,V}=c_{U,V}^{-1}$, and use $gf=g\circ f$. Every zero map $A\to B$ factors through $0$, so $L(0_{A,B})$ is the constant map with value $z_B$; functoriality also gives $L(f)(z_A)=z_B$. For linear maps $h:A\to U$ and $j:A\to V$, projection onto either factor gives
$c_{U,V}L(\langle h,j\rangle)(t)=(L(h)(t),L(j)(t))$.
Consequently $L(\langle h,j\rangle)(t)=q_{U,V}(L(h)(t),L(j)(t))$. More generally, for $f:U\to U'$ and $g:V\to V'$, comparison of the two projections gives
$L(f\oplus g)q_{U,V}(x,y)=q_{U',V'}(L(f)x,L(g)y)$.
These identities use only functoriality and the assumed bijectivity of $c$.

source.place: Tag 06I6 (lemma-linear-functor), construction and the omitted verification, expanded explicitly over a field.

proof.text: For each $V$ put $s_V(u,v)=u+v$, $m_a=a\,\mathrm{id}_V$, and define $x+y=L(s_V)q_{V,V}(x,y)$, $ax=L(m_a)x$ and $0=z_V$ as in the statement. Put $-x=L(m_{-1})x$. For $i_1(v)=(v,0)$ and $i_2(v)=(0,v)$, the first step gives $L(i_1)x=q(x,0)$ and $L(i_2)x=q(0,x)$. Since $s_Vi_1=s_Vi_2=\mathrm{id}$, we have $x+0=0+x=x$. If $\tau(u,v)=(v,u)$, comparison of projections gives $L(\tau)q(x,y)=q(y,x)$; since $s_V\tau=s_V$, addition is commutative. Finally $\langle\mathrm{id},m_{-1}\rangle$ followed by $s_V$ is zero. The first step therefore gives $x+(-x)=0$.

source.place: Tag 06I6 (lemma-linear-functor), construction and the omitted verification, expanded explicitly over a field.

proof.text:
To check associativity, set $T=(V\oplus V)\oplus V$ and $t=q_{V\oplus V,V}(q_{V,V}(x,y),z)$. If $r_1,r_2,r_3:T\to V$ are its three coordinate projections, then $L(r_1)t=x$, $L(r_2)t=y$, $L(r_3)t=z$. Set $h=\langle r_1,r_2\rangle$, $j=\langle r_2,r_3\rangle$. The pairing identity of step 1 gives
$L(\langle s_Vh,r_3\rangle)t=q(x+y,z)$ and $L(\langle r_1,s_Vj\rangle)t=q(x,y+z)$.
The two linear maps $s_V\langle s_Vh,r_3\rangle$ and $s_V\langle r_1,s_Vj\rangle$ agree, since both send $((u,v),w)$ to $u+v+w$. Applying $L$ and evaluating at $t$ proves $(x+y)+z=x+(y+z)$. Thus the operations of step 2 give an abelian group.

source.place: Tag 06I6 (lemma-linear-functor), construction and the omitted verification, expanded explicitly over a field.

proof.text:
For the scalar laws, $m_1=\mathrm{id}$ and $m_am_b=m_{ab}$ imply $1x=x$ and $a(bx)=(ab)x$ by functoriality; $m_0=0$ implies $0x=0$. For $\Delta(v)=(v,v)$, step 1 gives $L(\Delta)x=q(x,x)$. The identity $m_{a+b}=s_V\langle m_a,m_b\rangle$ therefore yields
$(a+b)x=L(s_V)q(ax,bx)=ax+bx$.
Here all displayed identities of maps hold in the original $k$-vector space, so use only the field and vector-space axioms already assumed.

source.place: Tag 06I6 (lemma-linear-functor), construction and the omitted verification, expanded explicitly over a field.

proof.text:
The remaining distributivity law follows from $m_as_V=s_V(m_a\oplus m_a)$. For $t=q_{V,V}(x,y)$, functoriality and step 1 give
$a(x+y)=L(m_as_V)t=L(s_V)L(m_a\oplus m_a)t=L(s_V)q(ax,ay)=ax+ay$.
Also $a0=0$ by step 1. Together with steps 2--4 these are all the axioms of a $k$-vector space on $L(V)$. No dimension or nonzero hypothesis on $V$ was used.

source.place: Tag 06I6 (lemma-linear-functor), construction and the omitted verification, expanded explicitly over a field.

proof.text:
For any linear $f:U\to V$, the identities $fs_U=s_V(f\oplus f)$ and $fm_a=m_af$ give
$L(f)(x+y)=L(s_V)L(f\oplus f)q_{U,U}(x,y)=L(s_V)q_{V,V}(L(f)x,L(f)y)=L(f)x+L(f)y$
and $L(f)(ax)=aL(f)x$. Step 1 gives preservation of zero, so every $L(f)$ is linear. Keeping the same object sets and maps therefore gives a functor to all $k$-vector spaces: its identity and composition laws are precisely those of $L$.

source.place: Tag 06I6 (lemma-linear-functor), construction and the omitted verification, expanded explicitly over a field.

proof.text:
For parallel $f,g:U\to V$, write $f+g=s_V\langle f,g\rangle$. The pairing identity of step 1 then gives, for every $x\in L(U)$,
$L(f+g)x=L(s_V)q_{V,V}(L(f)x,L(g)x)=L(f)x+L(g)x$.
Similarly $af=m_af$ implies $L(af)x=aL(f)x$. Equality on each $x$ proves the two asserted equalities of linear maps. These are exactly the additivity and scalar-linearity requirements in [def-weil-linear-functor], so the functor constructed in step 6 is $k$-linear.

source.place: Tag 06I6 (lemma-linear-functor), construction and the omitted verification, expanded explicitly over a field.

proof.text: Both components $L(p_U)$ and $L(p_V)$ of $c_{U,V}$ are linear by step 6; hence $c_{U,V}$ is linear for the componentwise structure on $L(U)\times L(V)$. It is bijective by hypothesis. Its inverse is linear directly: if $c(t)=u$ and $c(t')=u'$, then $c(t+t')=u+u'$ and $c(at)=au$; injectivity gives $c^{-1}(u+u')=t+t'$ and $c^{-1}(au)=at$. Thus it is a linear isomorphism, including when either space is zero.

source.place: Tag 06I6 (lemma-linear-functor), construction and the omitted verification, expanded explicitly over a field.

proof.text:
For uniqueness, take any structures with the properties in the statement, and denote their operations by $+'$, scalar multiplication by $\cdot'$ and zero by $0'$. The singleton $L(0)$ has its only possible vector-space structure. Since $L(0\to V)$ is linear, $0'=z_V$. Linearity on morphisms in the sense of [def-weil-linear-functor] forces
$L(a\,\mathrm{id}_V)=a\cdot' L(\mathrm{id}_V)=a\cdot'\mathrm{id}_{L(V)}$,
so $a\cdot'x=L(m_a)x$. Finally $s_V=p_1+p_2$ as maps $V\oplus V\to V$, hence $L(s_V)=L(p_1)+'L(p_2)$. Evaluating on the fixed element $q_{V,V}(x,y)$ yields $L(s_V)q(x,y)=x+'y$. Thus zero, scalar multiplication and addition agree with the constructed operations on every $L(V)$; additive inverses are then forced by the group law. Every arrow map was already fixed by $L$, so the lift is unique.

lean.statement: theorem productPreservingVectorFunctor_linearization {k : Type u} [Field k] (L : FGModuleCat.{v} k ⥤ Type w) (hzero : Unique (L.obj (FGModuleCat.of k PUnit.{v + 1}))) (hprod : ∀ U V : FGModuleCat.{v} k, Function.Bijective (vectorFunctorProductComparison L U V)) : ∃ (F : FGModuleCat.{v} k ⥤ ModuleCat.{w} k) (h : F ⋙ forget (ModuleCat.{w} k) = L), F.Additive ∧ F.Linear k ∧ (∀ G : FGModuleCat.{v} k ⥤ ModuleCat.{w} k, G ⋙ forget (ModuleCat.{w} k) = L → G.Additive → G.Linear k → G = F) ∧ (∀ V : FGModuleCat.{v} k, vectorFunctorLiftIdentification F h V 0 = L.map (0 : FGModuleCat.of k PUnit.{v + 1} ⟶ V) hzero.default) ∧ (∀ (V : FGModuleCat.{v} k) (x y : F.obj V), vectorFunctorLiftIdentification F h V (x + y) = L.map (prod.fst + prod.snd : V ⨯ V ⟶ V) ((Equiv.ofBijective (vectorFunctorProductComparison L V V) (hprod V V)).symm (vectorFunctorLiftIdentification F h V x, vectorFunctorLiftIdentification F h V y))) ∧ (∀ (V : FGModuleCat.{v} k) (a : k) (x : F.obj V), vectorFunctorLiftIdentification F h V (a • x) = L.map (a • 𝟙 V) (vectorFunctorLiftIdentification F h V x)) ∧ (∀ U V : FGModuleCat.{v} k, ∃ e : F.obj (U ⨯ V) ≃ₗ[k] (F.obj U × F.obj V), ∀ t : F.obj (U ⨯ V), e t = (F.map prod.fst t, F.map prod.snd t))
